second_order: mobilizing people to start a parrot
theme_note: These calls gather people to begin a parrot drawing; they vary between a general mobilization, a Party Parrot, coordinates, and joining a drawing already taking shape.

second_order: sharing pictures and coordinates so people can find the parrot
theme_note: The codes hold together as practical locating work: requesting or supplying a reference, naming landmarks or coordinates, showing a start, explaining zoom, and linking directly. What varies is whether the obstacle is knowing the design or finding its place.

second_order: marking pixels and reporting the parrot taking shape
theme_note: These passages make construction visible by marking a start, naming formed parts, clearing room, waiting for a legible shape, or restarting with new pixels; the reported stage varies from three pixels to a recognizable head.

second_order: working out how to place tiles
theme_note: Participants diagnose access problems and exchange fixes involving the app, browser, map, updates, and mobile access. The device-specific fixes vary, but the shared practice is getting would-be contributors able to place tiles.

The passages redirect contributors to a farther-along Party Parrot, exchange help through an allied-subs agreement, or ask allies to help another parrot. The direction and reciprocity vary, while the practice is moving help between efforts.

second_order: joking about parrots on the canvas
theme_note: These codes turn canvas developments into parrot jokes: renaming a Party Parrot as communist, claiming birds make communism work, laughing about two parrots, and mocking a defacer's avian anatomy. Their targets vary, but all make the shared drawing playful in locally ordinary bird language.

second_order: drawing borders without battling the neighbours
theme_note: Participants work out the edge and appearance of the parrot while trying not to fight adjacent work: black fill, grey or black outlines, a two-pixel border, and accepting purple over black if parrot pixels remain. The preferred colour changes, but preserving the bird and neighbour relations holds the codes together.
regrouped_from: split from trying to write r/parrots: border choices preserve the bird and avoid battles, whereas the name-writing exchange is about announcing the room

second_order: celebrating the parrot being finished and repaired
theme_note: These passages mark collective success after completion or repair. The immediate occasion varies between first completion, another successful fix, and later survival, but the doing is public celebration of the shared result.
regrouped_from: split from rebuilding and defending the Birb: these passages celebrate an outcome rather than report damage, call defenders, or perform repair

second_order: rebuilding and defending the Birb against damage
theme_note: The codes form one recurring practice around vulnerability: reporting loss, insisting the Birb stay, recreating it, answering protection calls, fixing defacement, and confronting an attacker. What varies is position in the sequence—loss report, rally, volunteered help, repair, attack claim, or rebuke—and whether the helper identifies with r/parrots.

second_order: trying and then dropping writing r/parrots
theme_note: Participants propose using nearby space to announce r/parrots, ask for help writing it, test whether it can fit, and drop the title to avoid disturbing neighbours and the bird. The codes vary from proposal to abandonment but belong to one worked-through naming plan.
regrouped_from: split from drawing borders without battling the neighbours: this exchange works out whether to label the bird, not what border the bird should have

second_order: keeping parrot links out of the spam filter
theme_note: A moderator asks contributors to avoid shortened links and a participant thanks them while pointing to the other effort post; together the exchange keeps coordination links visible.
All three submissions make the parrot an update-worthy object. One retains an update title and thread, while two retain only their titles because their bodies are gone.

second_order: turning a backup thread into talking about Baby's feet
theme_note: After the canvas backup call, participants discuss the pictured bird Baby: they ask about his feet, explain partial paralysis, compare birbs, ask his age, and call the curled feet a mystery. The details vary, but the common practice is shifting the retained thread into ordinary bird talk.

second_order: making and approving parrot pixel art after r/place
theme_note: The poster makes a pixel version of two Blackheaded clowns because of r/place, asks whether it belongs in the room, and receives approval. Creation, permission-seeking, and approval are different turns in one derivative-art practice.

second_order: not knowing what happened to the parrot
theme_note: This single code stands alone because it voices confusion inside a success thread rather than joining the celebration or describing defense.
